title: The Kings' Gate
journal: Never-Writes-Twice says the marked tower is one of the drowned spires off Lilmoth, and the divers of Bell Station will know which. This is the hunt of my order, the Toh-Reel-Ka, the Xeech-Leel's secret warriors. The Toh-Reel-Ka hunt the Eye of Argonia, the old kings' jewel that can heal every sick Hist, which lies at the Root, the place under the sea where the roots of every Hist meet, before the Unbound, the tribeless cult of Cuts-the-Old-Knot, can reach it. My own errand to Fort Chalkmoth may wait or come first. I'm to ask Meer-Tasi, the steward of Bell Station, on an islet east of Lilmoth, which tower the stone marks.
objectives: Ask Meer-Tasi, the steward of Bell Station, which tower the marker stone shows. (marker: Meer-Tasi, Sees-Below)

plan.going: The order hunts the Eye of Argonia, the old kings' jewel that can heal every sick Hist; it lies at the Root, where the roots of every Hist meet under the sea, and the Unbound want it first. The order's hunt goes on; the marker stone's tower is a drowned spire off Lilmoth. My own errand to Fort Chalkmoth is open beside it.
plan.next: Ask the steward of Bell Station which tower it is.
plan.ways: Either order with Fort Chalkmoth; one way here, a question.

answers: I am Toh-Wo, a Secret-Speaker of the Toh-Reel-Ka, the Xeech-Leel secret warriors. We hunt the Eye of Argonia, a jewel that can heal sick Hist, at the Root, before the Unbound cult of Cuts-the-Old-Knot gets it. The marker stone shows seven towers with one cut deeper, drowned spires off Lilmoth.
Ask Meer-Tasi, steward of Bell Station, which tower the stone marks (Sees-Below is also marked).
Talk to Meer-Tasi or Sees-Below; my Fort Chalkmoth errand can wait or come first. Sneaking is my favoured style.
I do not yet know what the Root and Eye really are, or what moans in the cellar of Fort Chalkmoth, or who the Collector is. I could find out by asking people and exploring.

title: The Kings' Gate
journal: The steward, Meer-Tasi, knew the cut tower at once: Teku-Sul Spire, the drowned tower nearest Lilmoth, whose great gate her divers have never forced. The dive is long. I need a Hist's blessing, a spell or potion of waterbreathing (she sells them) or an enchantment, unless I am Argonian; inside the tower there is air. I'm to dive to Teku-Sul and find the great gate. The drowned priests' attendants walk its east halls; I may fight them or slip past.
objectives: Find the great gate deep in Teku-Sul Spire. (marker: Door to Teku-Sul East Halls, Door to Teku-Sul Halls, Ghost of Sul-Xeeth)

plan.going: The marked tower is Teku-Sul Spire, under the sea; its great gate has never been forced.
plan.next: Dive to Teku-Sul and find the great gate beyond the east halls.
plan.ways: Breathe by a potion (bought or brewed), a blessing, a spell, an enchantment, or being Argonian; fight the attendants, turn them with Restoration, or pass them by stealth.

answers: Meer-Tasi says the cut tower is Teku-Sul Spire, nearest Lilmoth, a drowned tower whose great gate with three empty sockets has never been forced; a priest ghost stands before it. I serve the Toh-Reel-Ka hunting the Eye before the Unbound.
Dive to Teku-Sul Spire and find the great gate deep inside.

I am Argonian so I likely breathe water; otherwise buy waterbreathing from Meer-Tasi. Inside, attendants walk the east halls: fight or sneak past (I favour sneaking). I could also do Fort Chalkmoth first.

I do not know what the three sockets need (I carry a disc, keystone and eye-setting, which may fit), who the ghost Sul-Xeeth is, or what the Root is. I can find out by going there and talking to the ghost.

title: The Kings' Gate
journal: Before the great gate in Teku-Sul stands the ghost of a priest of the old kings, Sul-Xeeth. The gate has three empty sockets, one for each seal-stone the last king's priests cut, and only all three open it. One lies in the warden's vault at Blackrose Prison, one in the flooded vaults of Gemin, one in the deepest hall of Vorannuhl. I'm to tell Never-Writes-Twice in Nesh-Deeka's House in Helstrom.
objectives: Tell Never-Writes-Twice in Nesh-Deeka's House, Helstrom, what the ghost said. (marker: Never-Writes-Twice)

plan.going: The gate needs three seal-stones; I know where each lies.

answers: The ghost of Sul-Xeeth, priest of the last king, says the gate hides the way to the Root and the Eye. It needs three seal-stones, all set: one in the warden vault at Blackrose Prison, one in the flooded vaults of Gemin, one in the deepest hall of Vorannuhl. I work for the Toh-Reel-Ka.
Tell Never-Writes-Twice in Nesh-Deeka House, Helstrom, what the ghost said.
Go report to her now, or go after the stones myself first. I could also do the Fort Chalkmoth errand. I favour sneaking, which suits the prison vault.
I do not know where Gemin, Vorannuhl or Blackrose Prison are exactly, or what the Root and Eye really are. I can ask Never-Writes-Twice or check my map and journal.

title: The Kings' Gate
journal: Never-Writes-Twice made me a Reel-Ka, a Warrior of the order, and gave me its heavier armour, three hundred gold and a free bed in every Archwarden fort. Her orders are to take all three seal-stones before the Unbound do. I'm to fetch them from Blackrose Prison, Gemin and Vorannuhl, in any order; all three are marked, Blackrose the least dangerous and Vorannuhl the worst. My own errand to Fort Chalkmoth is still open.

plan.going: I am a Reel-Ka; the order wants all three seal-stones before the Unbound.
plan.next: Take the three stones from Blackrose Prison, Gemin and Vorannuhl, in any order (MN14 to MN16); Fort Chalkmoth is open too, my own errand.
plan.ways: Any order; the journal ranks them by danger.

answers: The quest is done: I am now Reel-Ka of the Toh-Reel-Ka, with heavier armour and 300 gold. The order wants all three seal-stones before the Unbound to open the Teku-Sul gate to the Root and use the Eye.
Fetch the stones from Blackrose Prison (easiest), Gemin and Vorannuhl (worst), in any order; Fort Chalkmoth errand is also still open.
Pick any order of the three sites, sneak or fight; or do Fort Chalkmoth first.
